newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro stocks close weak, data supports dollar.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro stocks close weak, data supports dollar.

text.p: European stock markets closed down near the day's lows on Friday, dragged lower by Wall Street, which extended recent losses on profit-taking and worries that U.S. Federal Reserve head Alan Greenspan might raise interest rates.
"People got a little bit nervous," said Charles Pradillo, Cowen and Co market analyst in New York. "I think there's just fears that Greenspan might be out there waiting in the wings to tighten."

Investors on both sides of the Atlantic were still wary of Greenspan's comments, in his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday, that higher U.S. interest rates might be needed to nip inflation in the bud.

Markets were already seen jittery over next week's U.S. jobs data, where a strong figure could underline fears of a possible U.S. rate hike. The second part of Greenspan's testimony was also seen as a market focus next week.

"I don't think he'll change the overall tone...his speech will be pretty hawkish, saying the Fed's about to push the trigger, but not just yet," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London.
The dollar was shaken in early trade as rumours of a possible delay in the launch of European economic and monetary union (EMU) boosted the mark.
The announcement of a downward revision in U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) data for the fourth 1996 quarter also saw the dollar slip back slightly against the mark before recovering.
But a batch of other U.S. data, most of which matched or exceeded expectations, buoyed the dollar, keeping market speculation on a U.S. rate increase on the boil, analysts said.

"Apart from the GDP, the rest of the data clearly showed the U.S. economy has got quite a momentum going in the early part of 1997, and that's going to keep the market on edge about a possible rate hike," said Stamenkovic. "That's giving good support to the dollar."
But traders said the market-friendly revision of fourth-quarter GDP was not enough to cheer bonds or stocks.
In Frankfurt the 30-share DAX index eased from Thursday's record as weakness in Japan and the United States and speculation over the fate of EMU combined to exert pressure on the market.
The German Bundesbank and Finance Ministry put the brakes on a rapid slide after denying a market rumour that Germany was about to issue a statement saying EMU would be delayed.

"The EMU issue should be over for the moment but it hasn't stopped people taking profits today. But there is still more upside in this market and we should see that next week," a dealer at a Bavarian bank said.
Thursday's 0.83 percent drop on Wall Street helped prompt the London stock market, Europe's busiest, to fall around three-quarters of a percentage point.
The Dow Jones industrial average was down a further 23 points, or a third of a percent, at 6,902 at midday in New York on Friday but above an earlier low of 6,868.
Sterling, meanwhile, dipped initially after the ruling Conservative Party suffered a crushing defeat in a parliamentary by-election in Britain, before reviving.
The markets had expected the opposition Labour Party to win the poll -- and the general election due by May -- and analysts said any downward move for the pound should be temporary.

"The effect of the by-election should not have a large impact because the unpopularity of the current government is hardly a surprise," said Klaus Baader, senior currency analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.

Markets, traditionally pro-Conservative, have usually seen the prospect of a Labour government as bearish but analysts said a decisive victory in the by-election could allay fears of uncertainty or a hung parliament after the general election.
French shares closed with a sharp loss, affected by the renewed slide in New York and profit-taking on the expiry of February futures.
Renault closed 13 percent higher at 146.90 francs after it announced the closure of its Belgian plant on Thursday.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was at 1.6887 marks and 120.74 yen, compared with 1.6892 and 120.70 in late European trade on Thursday.
Sterling traded around 2.7520 marks and $1.6312 versus 2.7484 and $1.6266 overnight.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended down 30.9 points or 0.71 percent at 4,308.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 ended down 21.85 points, or 0.83 percent, at 2,607.55.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended bourse floor trade 17.08 points lower at 3,259.64. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX was down 11.54 points, or 0.35 percent, at 3,261.04.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold ended London trading at $358.45, down $1.50 on the day. Silver was barely changed, ending two cents up at $5.27. Platinum ended down $2.00 on the day at $391.00, having earlier reached a high of $406.00 last touched in May 1996.
